title: Patents — Application, Specification, Publication, Examination and Opposition

content.overview: Patent procedure runs from a section 7 application and section 10 specification, through publication, a section 11B examination request, examination, and section 25 opposition, to grant. Filing and publication do not create the section 48 right. Each step has a trigger. Missing the examination request withdraws the application.
content.glance: Patents — Application, Specification, Publication, Examination and Opposition. Complete IPR treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective and Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body:
Patents — Application, Specification, Publication, Examination and Opposition sits within Intellectual Property Rights and is governed by Copyright Act, 1957; Trade Marks Act, 1999; Patents Act, 1970; Designs Act, 2000; Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999 and allied rules.

sections.body:
the claimant must establish subsistence, ownership or goodwill, infringement or passing off, validity and the requested remedy; the defendant may establish invalidity, fair dealing, honest use or other statutory defence

sections.body:

cases.name: R.G. Anand v. Deluxe Films
cases.facts: The dispute concerned alleged copying of a dramatic work into a film.
cases.issue: What test determines substantial copyright infringement of an idea or expression.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Copyright protects expression, not ideas, and infringement depends on substantial similarity assessed from the work as a whole.
cases.holding: The Court stated the governing comparison test.
cases.relevance: Use for copyright infringement and idea-expression distinction.

cases.name: Novartis AG v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court considered patentability of a pharmaceutical form under s. 3(d).
cases.issue: What enhanced efficacy threshold applies to a pharmaceutical derivative.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 3(d) requires the statutory enhanced-efficacy threshold and prevents evergreening without the required proof.
cases.holding: The patent claim was rejected under the statutory standard.
cases.relevance: Use for patentability exclusions and pharmaceutical patents.

cases.name: Cadila Health Care Ltd. v. Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd.
cases.facts: The parties used similar marks for pharmaceutical products.
cases.issue: How should deceptive similarity be assessed in pharmaceutical trademark disputes.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts must apply a stricter likelihood-of-confusion test for medicines because confusion may endanger public health.
cases.holding: The Court directed a careful comparison of the marks and circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for trademark confusion and public-interest analysis.

I. ISSUE AND JURISDICTION
Whether Patents — Application, Specification, Publication, Examination and Opposition applies to the stated facts and whether the chosen forum and remedy are maintainable.

II. GOVERNING RULE
Patents — Application, Specification, Publication, Examination and Opposition is governed by Copyright Act, 1957; Trade Marks Act, 1999; Patents Act, 1970; Designs Act, 2000; Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999 and allied rules. identify the right, registration status, relevant statute, filing or infringement date, limitation, forum and interim or final remedy.

III. INGREDIENT APPLICATION
Identify each condition, connect it to the evidence and answer the principal exception or defence. Apply BSA s. 63 to digital records where relevant and state the initial burden precisely.

IV. CONCLUSION
Grant, refuse or modify the relief only to the extent authorised by the governing law and proved record.

enhancement.definition: Patent procedure runs from a section 7 application and section 10 specification, through publication, a section 11B examination request, examination, and section 25 opposition, to grant. Filing and publication do not create the section 48 right.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Each step has a trigger. Missing the examination request withdraws the application.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The applicant files, publishes, requests examination, answers objections, and faces pre-grant opposition. Post-grant opposition lasts one year. A divisional application is used for a second invention. Fees and forms are rules.
enhancement.examples: An application is published and no examination is requested. It is treated as withdrawn. A pre-grant representation on prior publication is section 25.
enhancement.problemApplication: Match the facts to the section before using a neighbouring right. Do not invent a case ratio.
